stem: Which sentence states a feature that graphene and silicene share?
stimulus:
Notes on two materials:
• Graphene is a sheet of carbon only one atom thick.
• Graphene conducts electricity very well.
• Graphene was first isolated in 2004.
• Silicene is a sheet of silicon only one atom thick.
• Silicene breaks down quickly when exposed to air.
• Silicene was first made in 2012.
choices: Graphene and silicene are each a sheet of material only one atom thick.
Graphene was first isolated in 2004, whereas silicene was first made in 2012.
Graphene, a sheet of carbon only one atom thick, conducts electricity very well.
Graphene and silicene are each a sheet of carbon only one atom thick.
explanation: Scan the two blocks of notes for the one thing they both say: each material is a sheet only one atom thick. Choice A states that feature and covers both materials with a single phrase, 'Graphene and silicene are each.' On the real test, the 'emphasize a similarity' version of Rhetorical Synthesis questions starts with exactly this step: find the shared feature before you read the choices.

B.why: Every word here is accurate, but 'whereas' tells you the sentence is about a difference: the two materials appeared in different years. You picked a true detail instead of a shared feature.

C.why: This sentence mentions the shared feature, being one atom thick, but it only describes graphene. It never says silicene has that feature too, so it doesn't show a similarity.

D.why: The notes say silicene is made of silicon, not carbon. You found the right shared feature, but this sentence gets a detail wrong and ends up stating something false about silicene.

stem: Which sentence states a feature that Cooksonia and Archaeopteris share?
stimulus:
Notes on two fossil plants:
• Cooksonia lived about 430 million years ago.
• Cooksonia stood only a few centimeters tall.
• Cooksonia reproduced by releasing spores.
• Archaeopteris lived about 370 million years ago.
• Archaeopteris grew up to 30 meters tall.
• Archaeopteris reproduced by releasing spores.
choices: Cooksonia stood only a few centimeters tall, but Archaeopteris grew up to 30 meters.
Both Cooksonia and Archaeopteris reproduced by releasing spores into their surroundings.
Archaeopteris, which lived about 370 million years ago, reproduced by releasing spores.
Cooksonia and Archaeopteris both lived about 430 million years ago, in the same era.
explanation: The two blocks of notes differ on age and height. The only feature they share is the way the plants reproduced: by releasing spores. Choice B names both plants and uses 'both' to connect them to that feature. This is the first step on any 'emphasize a similarity' Rhetorical Synthesis question.

A.why: The difference in height is the most striking fact in the notes, and 'but' shows that this sentence is a contrast. It's true, but it describes a difference, not a similarity.

C.why: This sentence gives the shared feature for Archaeopteris only. Cooksonia is never mentioned, so a reader can't tell that the two plants have anything in common.

D.why: The notes give two different ages, 430 and 370 million years ago. This sentence uses 'both' correctly but applies it to a feature the plants don't share.

stem: Which sentence states a feature that ikat and batik share?
stimulus:
Notes on two textile methods:
• Ikat is a resist-dyeing method: parts of the threads are tightly tied off so dye cannot reach them.
• In ikat, the threads are dyed before the cloth is woven.
• Batik is a resist-dyeing method: parts of the cloth are covered in wax so dye cannot reach them.
• In batik, the cloth is dyed after it has been woven.
choices: In ikat the threads are dyed before weaving, while in batik the cloth is dyed after.
Batik is a method in which wax keeps dye from reaching certain parts of the cloth.
Ikat and batik are both methods that keep dye from reaching parts of a textile.
Ikat and batik are both methods in which wax keeps dye from reaching the cloth.
explanation: Both blocks of notes call the method 'resist-dyeing': in each one, something stops dye from reaching part of the material. Choice C states that one shared feature and applies it to both methods with 'both.' It leaves out the differences, such as tying versus wax and before versus after weaving, because the task is to state what they share.

A.why: This sentence is accurate and detailed, but 'while' shows that it's a contrast about when the dyeing happens. You picked the most informative sentence instead of the one that states a similarity.

B.why: This describes the resist feature for batik alone. Ikat is left out, so the sentence never shows that the two methods are alike.

D.why: Only batik uses wax. Ikat works by tying off threads. This sentence takes a detail that belongs to one method and wrongly gives it to both.

stem: Which sentence states a feature that the bus systems in Curitiba and Bogotá share?
stimulus:
Notes on two city bus systems:
• Curitiba, Brazil, opened its bus rapid transit system in 1974.
• Curitiba's buses run in lanes reserved only for buses.
• Bogotá, Colombia, opened its TransMilenio bus system in 2000.
• TransMilenio's buses run in lanes reserved only for buses.
choices: Curitiba opened its bus system in 1974, but Bogotá did not open TransMilenio until 2000.
Bogotá's TransMilenio, which opened in 2000, runs its buses in lanes reserved for buses.
Curitiba and Bogotá both opened their bus rapid transit systems in the same year, 1974.
The bus systems in Curitiba and Bogotá both run in lanes reserved only for buses.
explanation: The opening years differ, so they can't be the shared feature. What both blocks of notes say is that the buses run in lanes reserved only for buses. Choice D names both cities' systems and uses 'both' to connect them to that feature. On the real test, 'emphasize a similarity' questions reward you for finding this overlap first.

A.why: 'But' and 'not until' tell you this sentence is about a difference in timing. It's true, but it does the opposite of stating a similarity.

B.why: This sentence gives the shared feature, but only for Bogotá. Curitiba is never mentioned, so no similarity is stated.

C.why: The notes say Bogotá's system opened in 2000, not 1974. This sentence claims a shared feature that the notes directly contradict.
